<reason>CON's decisive move was introducing the somatic/germline distinction in the opening and never letting go of it: it directly exposed that PRO's strongest arguments (irreversible harm to non-consenting children, "the germline case is powerful") only justify banning germline editing, not the "strict prohibition" of all recreational genetic enhancement that the resolution demands. CON's pressure question ("why not simply ban germline and regulate somatic, as we already separate FDA-approved somatic therapy from banned germline editing?") went to the heart of this mismatch, and CON's self-regarding-consent principle (echoing existing law on minors, sterilization, and elective surgery) gave a clean, coherent line that PRO's own logic seemed to require. PRO's chief counter—that legalizing somatic enhancement would inevitably build infrastructure and normalization that erodes any germline ban—was a real and consistently pressed argument, but it remained a speculative causal chain never backed by a concrete mechanism, and CON's empirical counter (FDA-regulated somatic gene therapy has existed for years without germline creep) went largely unanswered except by assertion. PRO also let its "consent is fictional" argument fade after CON's "proves too much" rebuttal (rhinoplasty, teeth whitening, gym culture) went unaddressed in later rounds, and at points PRO's rebuttals blurred the somatic/germline line it needed to attack cleanly (e.g., calling somatic edits "heritable"). CON's closing directly neutralized PRO's opioid-market reframe by noting the opioid line held via enforcement without banning the whole pharmaceutical category—precisely the model CON was defending. Both sides suffered a clipped turn (B's opening, A's rebuttal 2), a roughly symmetric execution cost that does not change the outcome.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's opening somatic/germline distinction, sharpened via the "why not just ban germline and regulate somatic" pressure question and never squarely rebutted with a mechanism by PRO beyond speculative infrastructure-creep claims.</best_rebuttal>
